The four casualty states are §3.1 entities (casualty_state). Enumerating them is truthful and uniform across arms.
Vessel type is not a scored field. Permitted as realism — describes the world, implies nothing.

size_category IS a scored input: §7.1 draws the requirement band from it. Kept, and this is the one base line that touches a scored channel. It states the categories, never which band they map to, so Rule 2 holds.
draft is not a field (§6.1 names it explicitly). Descriptive only, scored by nothing.
cargo is not a field. Permitted as realism.
hazardous materials is not a field. Permitted as realism.

'All tanks may need checking ... before any cutting begins' is the strongest obligation implication in the file: a precondition nothing in v1 scores. Kept as realism because it is hedged and because it is domain knowledge the experiment is premised on supplying; flagged here because it is the closest base line to Rule 3. Revisit if V6 is ever scored.

'A fixed CO2 system may require a two-stage release with a pre-discharge alarm' — this is V4a's interlock stated as a requirement. V4a is in_v1: false (data/checks.json), so the line asserts an obligation NO v1 check scores, and it points at the exact construct a future check would measure. Rule 3. Remove.
Alcohol-resistant foam for polar solvents.

'The emergency fire pump's capacity may need confirming before committing a team' — plan.md §6.1 names this sentence verbatim as the banned example. Imperative, and `head`/`capacity confirmation` is unscoreable. Remove.
Fireboat monitors for boundary cooling.
Backdraft risk if a superheated space is opened.
Post-fire hull and stability reassessment.

'size and draft may scale the resources needed' — size is scored and this says resources scale with it. Kept: it states the direction, never the amount or which asset clears it, so the §7.2 trap survives (Rule 2). This is the single most load-bearing realism line in the file for the planner's chance of succeeding.
Cargo/hazmat as caution rather than approach change.

The generic resource catalogue ('Available resources may include harbor tugs ... foam concentrate'). Under grounded resources the LEDGER is the resource list, and this line directly contradicts mechanism line 4 ('Assets not listed in the ledger are not available'). Keeping it invites naming unlisted classes, which would inflate ¬V1 and ¬V3 as an artifact of the prompt — the P9 error class relocated to the input side. Replaced by the rendered ledger.

The generic crew catalogue. Same reason as 48: v1 ledgers carry no crew assets, so this line solicits assets that cannot resolve. §6.3's class exclusion means they would land on V3 rather than V1, but either way the failure would be the prompt's, not the planner's.

'Coordination may involve the vessel owner, local or flag authorities, a pollution reporting channel, or a commercial salvor.' §6.1 names owner/flag-authority coordination as a concept the world cannot express. It is also the nearest thing in the file to a hint about who to ask for more — Rule 1 territory, next to the ESCALATE affordance it must not script. Remove.

'Before writing the plan, ... answer the following about what is actually visible:' — elicits a preamble, which §6.2's format guard forbids ('no preamble before step 1'). It also spends output budget on a form. Removed; line 59 preserves the intent.

V3: same-class capacities combine approximately additively. Never says which total is reachable.
V2b (secondary): an asset does one task at a time. Kept although V2b is secondary — withholding the mechanism would make that secondary a trick question.
V2a: ETA = time from now until on scene and ready. Closest line to Rule 2; never says that time is the binding constraint.
V1: assets not listed are not available. Factual about the world, not an instruction about the output — which keeps it distinct from the banned honesty directive (§13 Q11).

'Include any assumptions, limitations, or requests alongside the steps.' Content-free, identical in every arm, states no trigger. Carries its own control: present at SURPLUS, where the ESCALATE rate IS the affordance's false-positive rate.
No preamble, no markdown tables, one step per line, do not restate the ledger. Structural in §10.1's taxonomy.
